items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: By the way, that's where I met Don Albert in Springfield.

ctx.x: Well, he had a little bit of air on the piano. But play. Ooh, he could play some piano. And never was sober. Never was sober. He stayed right there in the same hotel with us. He wake up in the morning and get drunk. Get drunk when he eat. Twelve o'clock he get drunk. Go to work he's drunk. Come from work he's drunk. But play. Never was late on the job. And never went to sleep. Never went to sleep. But he'd be drunk. Played everything you put in front of him and what you don't put in front of him he played. He was…

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: When I come back here, Don Albert took Alvin from me.

ctx.x: They had the band knife on the side of the bus? Yeah. What was the knife on the side of the bus? Handis, Louisiana Shakers. Handis or John Handis? No, Handis or John Handis. You keep the same men in the band in that tub? Yeah. Was there any chance? No, the same men.

When I come back here, Don Albert took Alvin from me. He had a regular job, I think. Alvin Alcorn went with him. And a trombone player. He went with him. And somebody just kept streaming out of the band. And he left and went with Don Albert.
Who was your top player on in the... I don't remember.
